tax.text: Income Taxes - Alliant Energy, IPL and WPL are subject to income taxes in various jurisdictions. Assumptions and judgments are made each reporting period to estimate income tax assets, liabilities, benefits and expenses. Judgments and assumptions are supported by historical data and reasonable projections. Significant changes in these judgments and assumptions could have a material impact on financial condition and results of operations. Alliant Energy’s and IPL’s critical assumptions and judgments for 2024 included estimates of qualifying deductions for repairs expenditures, allocation of mixed service costs and state depreciation, and costs related to retirement or removal of depreciable property due to the impact of Iowa rate-making principles on such property-related differences. Critical assumptions and judgments also include projections of future taxable income used to determine the ability to utilize federal credit carryforwards prior to their expiration. Refer to Note 1 1 for further discussion of tax matters.

net.text: Alliant Energy’s Utilities and Corporate Services net income decreased by $2 million in 2024 compared to 2023. The decrease was primarily due to an asset valuation charge for IPL’s Lansing Generating Station as a result of the IUC order for IPL’s retail electric rate review, estimated temperature impacts on retail electric and gas sales, restructuring and voluntary separation charges, an ARO charge allocated to the steam business at IPL due to the revised CCR Rule, higher depreciation and financing expenses, and lower AFUDC. These items were partially offset by higher revenue requirements from capital investments.

ocf.text: • Cash Flows From Operating Activities - Alliant Energy, IPL and WPL currently expect an increase in future cash flows from operating activities resulting from the transfer of future renewable tax credits to other corporate taxpayers pursuant to the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022. da.text: • Depreciation and Amortization Expense - Alliant Energy, IPL and WPL currently expect an increase in depreciation and amortization expense in 2025 compared to 2024 due to capital projects placed in service in 2024 and 2025, and updated electric depreciation rates for IPL effective October 1, 2024.

Electric.text: • In March 2025, WPL filed a retail electric and gas rate review with the PSCW for the 2026/2027 forward-looking Test Period. The key drivers for the filing include revenue requirement impacts of increasing electric and gas rate base, including wind refurbishment projects, energy storage, existing natural gas-fired EGU improvements, solar generation costs incurred that exceed the construction cost estimates previously approved by the PSCW, and electric and gas distribution investments. The filing requested approval for WPL to implement increases in annual rates for its retail electric and gas customers of $120 million and $9 million in 2026, respectively, with any granted rate changes expected to be effective on January 1, 2026. WPL’s filing also requested approval to implement an additional increase in annual rates for its retail electric and gas customers of $82 million and $5 million in 2027, respectively, with any granted rate changes expected to be effective on January 1, 2027. WPL also requested a return on common equity of 9.9% and to implement a common equity component of its regulatory capital structure of 55.5% in 2026 and 55.3% in 2027.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
